title: Check findings
description: A model's check of a text the companion wrote — by the editor after an answer, or by the reviewer on request — against the evidence lines its request quoted, as the arguments of its check_findings call. Each statement the request numbered is accounted for: by a finding, as supported, or as skipped. A model's reading of a model's text, never verified fact and never evidence.

supported.description: The statements found supported as worded by the lines given.

skipped.description: The statements with nothing to check: an ask of the customer, a step to take, or a question.

corrected.description: The editor's corrected text of the whole answer, where it changed wording or a citation for a finding that is not an anchor, its statements as many and in the same order; the reviewer writes none.

statement.description: A statement by the ID the request gave it, such as s3.

lines.description: Evidence lines among those the request quoted: e12, e12:41 or e12:41-58.

finding.description: What is wrong with one statement, quoting its words at fault.

kind.description: unsupported: nothing given holds it; overstated: the lines hold a weaker statement; misattributed: attributed or inferred stated as observed, or the wrong source; listing_as_state: a file listing cited for what runs, ran or is mounted; unestablished_link: a causal or temporal link the lines do not make; qualifier_dropped: an earlier statement's qualifier gone (the editor only); citation_mismatch: the cited lines exist and do not say it, and where other quoted lines do the editor corrects the citation to them; undetermined: the lines given cannot settle it; certainty: certainty or causal wording in the writer's own voice beyond what the lines and their attribution justify.

quote.description: The words at fault, exactly as the statement has them.

suggested.description: The maximum justified wording: a phrase on the wording ladder, an attributed phrase, or unresolved; on an anchor, what fulfils it.

alternative.description: The reviewer's only: the strongest material alternative still consistent with the record, or none where none is meaningful.

discriminator.description: The reviewer's only: the evidence that would distinguish the claim from the alternative, and whether it is given.

anchor.description: The editor's only: true where the finding needs the conversation — who said it, or lines the request did not quote — and is left to the main model's revision; an anchor says in suggested what fulfils it.
